question: Does the high AWGN setting explain away the high-iteration decoder events?

verified.noise_semantics: Absolute receiver noise, not continuously adjusted to maintain 40 dB after propagation.

estimator_source.method: After estimated timing-slope compensation, RSRP is squared magnitude of averaged complex pilot estimates; EPRE is average squared pilot magnitude. n0=EPRE-RSRP; SNR=10log10(RSRP/n0).
estimator_source.implication: Channel variation or residual distortion across pilot estimates contributes to the residual; this is not a direct readback of injected AWGN power.

conclusion: High-iteration PDSCH decoding is measured; attribution of the difficult decoder input to genuinely poor propagation/noise is not established. Fixed noise and roughly 14 dB path gain loss alone do not explain a 40 dB setting turning into -2.5 dB reported PDSCH SNR.
remaining_question: Separate channel/UE-estimation residuals from actual waveform distortion using aligned boundary IQ around the event; existing first-buffer captures do not span this event.
